newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama insists privatization process transparent.
newsitem.headline: Panama insists privatization process transparent.

text.p: Panamanian Foreign Minister Ricardo Arias dismissed Monday complaints that Panama's privatization processes have not been transparent.

"It is incomprehensible that a reduced number of incidences could cause the perception that Panama lacks an adequate environment for foreign investment," Arias said in a written statement released Monday.

U.S. Ambassador to Panama William Hughes said recently in a letter to Commerce Minister Raul Arango that several U.S. senators have received complaints from American companies alleging unfair treatment in Panama.

Hughes outlined seven cases where U.S. firms had complained that after winning the bids, the government either reneged on the offers or changed the bid agreements, including a decision last year to revoke a telecommunications license soon after it was awarded.

"I urge your Government to take immediate steps to deal with the U.S. investors' complaints and to turn this growing negative perception," Hughes said in the letter published in national daily La Prensa over the weekend.

Panama generated controversy last year when it rejected bids from four international companies to build what would be the country's second-biggest dam in Chiriqui province. The government opened a new bidding process and is expected to award a contract soon.

Hong Kong-based Hutchison Whampoa Ltd won a concession to develop two ports in an auction that was criticized by foreign investors and diplomats for opening sealed bids and changing regulations in the privatization process.
